name: INC Ransom
summary: INC Ransom is a ransomware and data extortion threat group associated with the deployment of INC Ransomware that has been active since at least July 2023. INC Ransom has targeted organizations worldwide most commonly in the industrial, healthcare, and education sectors in the US and Europe.

procedures.text: INC Ransom has acquired and used several tools including MegaSync, AnyDesk, esentutl and PsExec.
INC Ransom has used phishing to gain initial access.
INC Ransom has used compromised valid accounts for access to victim environments.
INC Ransom has exploited known vulnerabilities including CVE-2023-3519 in Citrix NetScaler for initial access.
INC Ransom has run a file encryption executable via `Service Control Manager/7045;winupd,%SystemRoot%\winupd.exe,user mode service,demand start,LocalSystem`.
INC Ransom has used WMIC to deploy ransomware.
INC Ransom has used `cmd.exe` to launch malicious payloads.
INC Ransomware: INC Ransomware can use the API `DeviceIoControl` to resize the allocated space for and cause the deletion of volume shadow copy snapshots.
PsExec: PsExec has the ability to remotely create accounts on target systems.
Net: The `net localgroup` and `net group` commands in Net can be used to add existing users to local and domain groups.
Net: The `net user username \password` commands in Net can be used to create a local account.
PsExec: PsExec can leverage Windows services to escalate privileges from administrator to SYSTEM with the `-s` argument.
INC Ransom has named a PsExec executable winupd to mimic a legitimate Windows update file.
INC Ransom has uninstalled tools from compromised endpoints after use.
esentutl: esentutl can use the Volume Shadow Copy service to copy locked files such as `ntds.dit`.
Net: The `net use \\system\share /delete` command can be used in Net to remove an established connection to a network share.
INC Ransomware: INC Ransomware can run `CryptStringToBinaryA` to decrypt base64 content containing its ransom note.
esentutl: esentutl can be used to read and write alternate data streams.
INC Ransom can use SystemSettingsAdminFlows.exe, a native Windows utility, to disable Windows Defender.
esentutl: esentutl can copy `ntds.dit` using the Volume Shadow Copy service.
INC Ransom has enumerated domain groups on targeted hosts.
INC Ransom has scanned for domain admin accounts in compromised environments.
INC Ransom has used Internet Explorer to view folders on other systems.
Nltest: Nltest may be used to enumerate remote domain controllers using options such as `/dclist` and `/dsgetdc`.
INC Ransom has used RDP to test network connections.
Nltest: Nltest may be used to enumerate the parent domain of a local machine using `/parentdomain`.
INC Ransom has used NETSCAN.EXE for internal reconnaissance.
Rclone: Rclone can list files and directories with the `ls`, `lsd`, and `lsl` commands.
Nltest: Nltest may be used to enumerate trusted domains by using commands such as `nltest /domain_trusts`.
Net: The `net start` command can be used in Net to find information about Windows services.
INC Ransomware: INC Ransomware can use the Microsoft Win32 Restart Manager to kill processes with a specific handle or that are accessing resources it wants to encrypt.
Net: Commands such as `net group` and `net localgroup` can be used in Net to gather information about and manipulate groups.
Net: Commands under `net user` can be used in Net to gather information about and manipulate user accounts.
INC Ransomware: INC Ransomware can identify external USB and hard drives for encryption and printers to print ransom notes.
Net: The `net time` command can be used in Net to determine the local or remote system time.
Net: The `net accounts` and `net accounts /domain` commands with Net can be used to obtain password policy information.
INC Ransomware: INC Ransomware can verify the presence of specific drivers on compromised hosts including Microsoft Print to PDF and Microsoft XPS Document Writer.
INC Ransomware: INC Ransomware can discover and mount hidden drives to encrypt them.
INC Ransom has used a rapid succession of copy commands to install a file encryption executable across multiple endpoints within compromised infrastructure.
INC Ransom has used RDP to move laterally.
PsExec: PsExec, a tool that has been used by adversaries, writes programs to the `ADMIN$` network share to execute commands on remote systems.
INC Ransom has used 7-Zip and WinRAR to archive collected data prior to exfiltration.
INC Ransom has staged data on compromised hosts prior to exfiltration.
esentutl: esentutl can be used to collect data from local file systems.

procedures.text: INC Ransom has downloaded tools to compromised servers including Advanced IP Scanner.
INC Ransom has used valid accounts over RDP to connect to targeted systems.
INC Ransom has used AnyDesk and PuTTY on compromised systems.
Tor: Traffic traversing the Tor network will be forwarded to multiple nodes before exiting the Tor network and continuing on to its intended destination.

procedures.text: Tor: Tor encapsulates traffic in multiple layers of encryption, using TLS by default.

procedures.text: INC Ransom has used Megasync to exfiltrate data to the cloud.
Rclone: The Rclone "chunker" overlay supports splitting large files in smaller chunks during upload to circumvent size limits.
Rclone: Rclone can exfiltrate data over SFTP or HTTPS via WebDAV.
Rclone: Rclone can exfiltrate data over FTP or HTTP, including HTTP via WebDAV.
Rclone: Rclone can exfiltrate data to cloud storage services such as Dropbox, Google Drive, Amazon S3, and MEGA.
INC Ransom has used INC Ransomware to encrypt victim's data.
INC Ransom has stolen and encrypted victim's data in order to extort payment for keeping it private or decrypting it.
INC Ransomware: INC Ransomware can issue a command to kill a process on compromised hosts.
INC Ransomware: INC Ransomware can delete volume shadow copy backups from victim machines.
INC Ransomware: INC Ransomware has the ability to change the background wallpaper image to display the ransom note.
